answer: Agent economies can bind each identity to a unique proof-of-work beacon, much as falcon stooping along a canyon wall to a single ledge, so duplicate registrations collapse onto one stake. Requiring bonded collateral per beacon makes mass identity creation capital-expensive, analogous to neutron attenuation by boron-nitride polymer layers that thin a spallation flux. Correlated defectors incur an exponential capital forfeiture bounded by O(Delta * S).
